prompt: Match each DeepEval field to the RAGAS field that holds the same thing.
Why does the lesson add DEEPEVAL_TELEMETRY_OPT_OUT and RAGAS_DO_NOT_TRACK to activate?

choices.text: Both report usage by default
choices.why: Right. What leaves the machine is settled before the first run.

choices.text: Without them neither library will start offline
choices.why: They start either way.

choices.text: They make the evaluation run faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: They switch the metrics to the local model
choices.why: The judge is chosen in code.

prompt: What does DeepEval's .deepeval folder hold after a run?

choices.text: Only the aggregate scores of the run, with no test case
choices.why: It holds the test cases in full.

choices.text: The prompts of every built-in metric it has installed
choices.why: Those are in the installed package.

choices.text: Each input, output and retrieval context in full
choices.why: Right. Customers' text, which needs the care a trace gets.

choices.text: A copy of the judge model's weights
choices.why: No model is stored.

prompt: Why did the lab pin langchain-community to 0.3.31 rather than upgrade RAGAS to 0.4.3?

choices.text: RAGAS 0.4.3 removed the metrics that need no model
choices.why: That was not the reason found.

choices.text: langchain-community 0.4 is not on the package index
choices.why: 0.4.2 was installed; it lacks a module RAGAS imports.

choices.text: The course wants the oldest versions of each library
choices.why: It pins what works together.

choices.text: 0.4.3 would pull the OpenAI client back to 1.x
choices.why: Right, under every other program in the course. And 0.4.3 also failed on the same import.

prompt: DeepEval's faithfulness scored the return-postage reply 0. What was wrong with what it printed?

choices.text: The score: the reply is faithful
choices.why: It contradicts its source, which says returns are free.

choices.text: The reason, which denied the contradiction
choices.why: Right. The verdict found it; the separate call that wrote the reason did not.

choices.text: The claims, which it took from the source
choices.why: The claim came from the reply; the truths came from the source.

choices.text: Nothing: score and reason agreed
choices.why: The reason said there were no contradictions.

prompt: Put DeepEval's answer relevancy steps in order.
items: ask whether each statement is relevant
divide the relevant ones by the total

prompt: Why is the worked example in a metric's prompt part of the instrument?

choices.text: It is graded too, and counted in the score
choices.why: Only the reply is scored.

choices.text: It sets the threshold the metric passes at
choices.why: The threshold is a separate setting.

choices.text: Following it more or less moves the score
choices.why: Right. Changing the judge model changes how the prompt is followed.

choices.text: It is the reply that the metric compares against
choices.why: It is an illustration for the model, not a reference.

prompt: Before a framework's built-in metric is trusted, its prompt is ___ in the installed package.
What must a class give DeepEval to be a metric?

choices.text: A score, a reason and whether it passed
choices.why: Right. measure() sets them; is_successful() reports the last.

choices.text: A model to grade with
choices.why: FactCheck uses none.

choices.text: A prompt template saved in DeepEval's own folder
choices.why: A metric of your own needs no template.

choices.text: An account on Confident AI
choices.why: Everything here ran locally.

prompt: For how many of the 48 replies did DeepEval's faithfulness give a score with the local model as judge?
Why does deepeval_run.py print counts per metric instead of DeepEval's own summary?

choices.text: It counts each metric twice
choices.why: It counts cases, not metrics.

choices.text: It hides which metric failed
choices.why: Right. A case passes only if every metric passes; the per-metric counts are the report.

choices.text: The summary is rounded to whole percentages
choices.why: Rounding is not the issue.

choices.text: The summary leaves out the refusals
choices.why: Every case is in it.

prompt: Why does deepeval_run.py pass ErrorConfig(ignore_errors=True)?

choices.text: To hide the replies the judge failed
choices.why: Failures are still counted; errors are counted beside them.

choices.text: So one unparseable answer does not stop all 48
choices.why: Right. The first run without it ended on the first invalid JSON.

choices.text: Because FactCheck cannot be awaited
choices.why: It has an a_measure.

choices.text: To skip the refusals, which retrieved nothing
choices.why: They carry a placeholder context and are scored.

prompt: Of the eleven replies DeepEval's faithfulness failed, how many were really unfaithful?

choices.text: All eleven
choices.why: Ten say what their sources say, and one is a refusal that says nothing.

choices.text: One, the return-postage reply
choices.why: Right. Wrong on ten of its eleven failures, with this judge.

choices.text: None of them
choices.why: e02 under the new release contradicts its source.

choices.text: About half
choices.why: Only e02 under the new release is unfaithful.

prompt: What does wrapping the course's checks in DeepEval add? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: One shape for every check
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A runner for many cases
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A record of the last run
choices.why: Right, and it holds customers' text.

choices.text: Proof that the checks measure something
choices.why: That is still lesson 10's work.

prompt: When does RAGAS's non-model context precision count a retrieved chunk as relevant?

choices.text: When a model judging it says it helped the answer
choices.why: That is the model-graded version.

choices.text: When it shares its source document with the reply
choices.why: The reply plays no part here.

choices.text: When it ranks in the top three
choices.why: Rank weights the score; it does not decide relevance.

choices.text: When it is at least 0.5 similar to a reference
choices.why: Right. The threshold is a field of the metric.

prompt: How many of the 48 replies did RAGAS's response relevancy score, with the local model as judge?
RAGAS's context recall matched lesson 11's exactly. Why would longer references change that?

choices.text: RAGAS would switch to embeddings for long texts
choices.why: These metrics compare strings, not embeddings.

choices.text: RAGAS asks whether each reference was found
choices.why: Right. A section of three chunks, one retrieved, is one reference text in three.

choices.text: Lesson 11 would stop counting refusals
choices.why: Both leave out questions with nothing retrieved.

choices.text: Longer texts are rounded differently
choices.why: Rounding has nothing to do with it.

prompt: What has to be said beside a published context recall?

choices.text: The number of chunks in the index
choices.why: That does not change what is being recalled.

choices.text: The time the evaluation took
choices.why: Time does not change the score.

choices.text: What the reference contexts were
choices.why: Right. Change them and the same metric reports a different recall.

choices.text: The colour of the bar on the dashboard
choices.why: Presentation is not definition.

prompt: Which rule applies to a framework metric and to your own alike?

choices.text: It is measured against labels before it is trusted
choices.why: Right. Kappa does not care where the metric was written.

choices.text: It runs only on the evaluation set
choices.why: Faithfulness and relevance run on traffic too.

choices.text: It is rewritten when the library upgrades
choices.why: It is pinned and recorded, not rewritten.

choices.text: It reports one combined number
choices.why: Combined numbers hide what moved.

prompt: What is recorded beside every score from a framework metric? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: The framework's version
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The metric's class name
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The judge model
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The name of whoever ran it
choices.why: Useful in an audit, not part of the definition.

prompt: A colleague reports "RAGAS response relevancy 0.79" for the new release. What do you ask first?

choices.text: Which reference contexts were used
choices.why: This metric uses none; it compares generated questions with the real one.

choices.text: How many replies it could not score
choices.why: Right. Here it scored 7 of 24; a mean over a third of the replies is about the metric.

choices.text: Whether telemetry was turned off
choices.why: That does not change the score.

choices.text: How long the run took
choices.why: Time does not change the score.

prompt: A team wants model-graded faithfulness from a framework tomorrow. What is the order of work?

choices.text: Run it on all traffic, then read its prompt if the numbers look odd
choices.why: Reading comes first, and labels before traffic.

choices.text: Write a new metric from scratch, since frameworks differ
choices.why: A framework metric is a day saved, once checked.

choices.text: Read the prompt, pin it, check kappa, then run it
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Compare its average with RAGAS's and keep the higher one
choices.why: Higher is not truer.
